You are comparing two drafts written from the same brief. Read no other file, and do not run commands or browse; judge only the text below.

Brief: Write the README's opening paragraph and its Install and update section for the `tidy-hooks` plugin.

<<<DRAFT A
`tidy-hooks` is a Claude and Codex plugin that blocks `git commit` when staged files contain merge markers.

## Install and update

### Claude

Add the marketplace, then install the plugin:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add example/tidy
claude plugin install tidy-hooks@tidy
```

To update the plugin, run:

```sh
claude plugin update tidy-hooks@tidy
```

### Codex

Add the marketplace, then install the plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add example/tidy
codex plugin add tidy-hooks@tidy
```

Review and trust the plugin hooks. Codex skips them until you do.

To update, run the following command, then restart Codex:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade tidy
```

If Node.js is missing, the hook lets commits proceed.
DRAFT A>>>

<<<DRAFT B
`tidy-hooks` is a Claude and Codex plugin that blocks `git commit` when staged files contain merge markers. The hook fails open: if Node.js is missing, commits proceed.

## Install and update

### Claude

Install:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add example/tidy
claude plugin install tidy-hooks@tidy
```

Update:

```sh
claude plugin update tidy-hooks@tidy
```

### Codex

Install:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add example/tidy
codex plugin add tidy-hooks@tidy
```

Codex skips plugin hooks until you review and trust them.

Update:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade tidy
```

Then restart Codex.
DRAFT B>>>

items.text:
I'm comparing the two versions side by side. Both say the same thing, but A puts the Node.js fail-open note at the end of the Codex section, where it doesn't belong since it applies to both hosts. B puts it in the opening, which fits better. A's update instruction comes before the command and reads clearly, and its "Review and trust the plugin hooks" line is good because it leads with the action.

I'm weighing the labels now: B's "Install:" and "Update:" are terse but still workable. Both versions read fine overall, though B seems a bit stronger because its fail-open note sits where it belongs, while A's placement might make it look Codex-only. I'm leaning toward B.
